design:
## Design tests

The rules were read blind in seven whole test scenes among other events (`vision/design_tests_v021.md`): a garden with the fence being painted, someone watering by can and a dog playing; a garden with the washing being hung, a dig and a kick; a busy park by the pond with the duck feeding, a runner, the bird feeding, a dog walker and a photographer; a park with someone fishing; a playground with a kick beside the sandpit; a busy street; and a busy garden with the blocked hose. Every rule read as meant. No reader saw a worker's vest in the garden, a hose reel or a spare can beside someone watering, a bowl away from a dog, a head among the hung washing ("a man ... stretching up to peg a white T-shirt onto a washing line, where a pair of blue jeans already hangs"), a figure in the cattails, walkers on each other's shoulders, or a kick at the sandpit ("heading off to the right, away from the other children"). The can's water fell "onto the middle of the flower bed". Two readers said people at the pond's front edge overlap its outline, each adding that their feet are on the grass, "so they read as standing at the bank". Nothing in the test scenes called for another change; one test scene had to be split, since duck feeding and fishing together in a tier-4 park placed in none of four seeds.
intro: None of the v0.20 oddities that revision 19 addressed came back in the eighteenth screen: no worker's vest in a garden, no dog bowl away from a dog, no head among the washing, no spare hose reel or can beside someone watering, no figure in the cattails, no walkers on each other's shoulders, no kick at the sandpit. 738 of 744 scored items had full marks, and the probes' unintended oddities fell by half (68 to 34). But one item of the set was misread, the first since v0.11: in the tier-4 street a woman watering a planter box with a frying pan, the pan held up against a grey shop door, read as "a grey watering can", so its contradiction was missed; in the same picture a teenager jumping for joy read as standing with his arms up. With a ladder that one probe reader could not tell standing from lying flat, three templates fall short of the gate, each of them read in full in v0.20 and in two of its three pictures here: 61 of 64 pass (64 in v0.20). The set scored 0.989 over all items (0.998 in v0.20); its inferences rose to 1.00 and its oddities fell from 1.2 to 1.1 per picture. `vision/flaws_v021.md` lists the three, and the square wheel's second "round wheel inside a square frame", for v0.22.
screen: Across all 65 pictures 6 of 744 scored items fell short of full marks (2 of 746 in v0.20): four half points, and a zero and a misread on the same frying pan. In the set, all in the tier-4 street: the pan, held up face-on at a raised planter box against the slate-grey shop door, read as "a grey watering can" ("a grey can or pot", "nothing looks physically impossible"), its stream "running down the side of the planter"; and a teenager jumping for joy in front of the fruit stall, his feet about 40 px above his shadow, read as standing "with both arms up, smiling", "cheering, celebrating, stretching or dancing". In the probes, a ladder on the open grass, its top just below the foot of a lamp post, was "standing up at a lean ... or lying flat" (two half points), and the square-wheeled wheelbarrow was once more "a square dark frame with a spoked wheel inside it". One scorer gave no half point at all and listed nine hedged items it credited in full. Unintended oddities fell from 26 to 24 in the set and from 68 to 34 in the probes. What the readers noticed: a sprinkler's hose rising "straight up out of the bottom edge like a stiff pipe" (two probes); hoses hard to follow near the hand or under a dog's paws (three probes); extra trip stories (a boy with an ice cream by a wheelbarrow's handles, a reading walker by a sleeping cat or a bicycle, a runner heading for the flower bed); slide chutes ending above the grass; and the older ones (goats, leaves under no tree, the tilted empty swing, a runner in a dress).
redrawn: The two v0.20 half points read better: the dropped ice cream at 1.00 over 12 items in three pictures (0.969 in v0.20), the square wheel at 0.967 over 15 items in five (0.944), its one half point the same "round wheel inside a square frame" reading as in v0.20. Every template whose placement revision 19 changed read with full marks: the painter with no worker's vest and no washing behind the boards, the washing being hung beside the jeans alone, the watering can with no reel beside it, the hose drawn in front of the flower bed, the blocked hose with no spare can, the sprinkler with nobody in front of its spray, the duck feeding and the fishing off the cattails, the dog walker and the reader off other figures' shoulders, and the kick clear of the sandpit.
gate: Every template was screened in at least three pictures (54 in three, 4 in four, 4 in five, 1 in six, 1 in seven), and 61 of 64 pass. The three that fall short each read in full in v0.20 and in two of their three pictures here: the frying pan (one misread), the jumper (one half point) and the ladder leaning on nothing (two half points in one probe). About five templates of the gate's movement between screens is reader variance (the v0.9 retest); two of the three, though, have a cause in their picture to fix (the pan against a grey door, the jumper's small gap above his shadow in front of the stall), and the ladder's open-grass probe gives the bench a case to try.
inspection: Building and inspecting the set and the probes found four more things, all fixed before the screen. The first build stopped on a garden that paired watering by can with the blocked hose: dropping the reel from beside the can had left the hose with no reel, so watering by can now never shares a picture with a hose. The first tier-4 park had a goat grazing just in front of a sprinkler's arcs, as if in the spray; nobody may now stand in front of the spray or its box, and the park was searched again. Two garden probes had a hose reel and a spare watering can beside the sprinkler, whose own hose runs off the picture; they were rebuilt without either. And hosing the flowers had stopped placing at all: its hose was a fifth hidden behind the flower bed, and with heads kept clear of the washing there was nowhere else for the waterer to stand, so the hose is now drawn in front of the bed and no washing hangs beside it. Hosing and fishing were then in no screened picture, so each went into three probes beside the templates of the probes they replaced, keeping the screen at 65 pictures.
calib: The duck feeding's cue salience moved by +0.026 and the frying pan's by +0.02 (measured in 15 scenes instead of 12); every other template's by at most 0.01.
